subject: physics
pattern: This chapter is worth about 9 to 11 marks: a 1-mark definition or law, a 2-mark numerical or statement, 3-mark derivations (field at the centre of a circular loop, force between parallel wires, solenoid by Ampere's law) and a 5-mark question on the cyclotron, torque on a current loop or the moving coil galvanometer. Examiners expect Biot-Savart or Ampere's law stated, the diagram described, and direction rules (Fleming's left-hand, right-hand thumb) mentioned.

questions.answer: One tesla is the magnetic field strength at which a charge of 1 C moving at 1 m s$^{-1}$ perpendicular to the field experiences a force of 1 N. Equivalently, it is the field that exerts a force of 1 N on a 1 m conductor carrying 1 A placed perpendicular to the field. 1 T = 1 N A$^{-1}$ m$^{-1}$.

questions.q: Write the expression for the Lorentz force on a charge q moving with velocity v in electric field E and magnetic field B.
questions.answer: $\vec{F} = q\left(\vec{E}+\vec{v}\times\vec{B}\right)$. The magnetic part $q(\vec{v}\times\vec{B})$ has magnitude $qvB\sin\theta$ and is perpendicular to both v and B, so it does no work on the charge.
The line integral of the magnetic field around any closed path is $\mu_0$ times the total current enclosed by the path: $\oint\vec{B}\cdot d\vec{l} = \mu_0 I$.

questions.q: Define the ampere on the basis of the force between two parallel current-carrying conductors.
questions.answer: One ampere is that steady current which, when flowing in each of two infinitely long, thin, straight parallel conductors placed 1 m apart in vacuum, produces between them a force of $2\times10^{-7}$ N per metre of length. This follows from $\frac{F}{l} = \frac{\mu_0I_1I_2}{2\pi d}$ with $\mu_0 = 4\pi\times10^{-7}$ T m A$^{-1}$.

questions.q: State the Biot-Savart law and write it in vector form.
questions.answer: The magnetic field $d\vec{B}$ at a point due to a small current element $I\,d\vec{l}$ is directly proportional to the current and the length of the element, proportional to the sine of the angle between $d\vec{l}$ and the line joining the element to the point, and inversely proportional to the square of the distance r. $d\vec{B} = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{I\,d\vec{l}\times\vec{r}}{r^3}$, with magnitude $\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{I\,dl\sin\theta}{r^2}$.

questions.q: An electron moves with a speed of $3\times10^{7}$ m s$^{-1}$ perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of 0.5 T. Find the radius of its circular path. ($m = 9.1\times10^{-31}$ kg, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}$ C)
questions.answer: The magnetic force provides the centripetal force: $evB = \frac{mv^2}{r}$, so $r = \frac{mv}{eB} = \frac{9.1\times10^{-31}\times3\times10^{7}}{1.6\times10^{-19}\times0.5} = \frac{2.73\times10^{-23}}{8\times10^{-20}} = 3.4\times10^{-4}$ m (about 0.34 mm).

questions.q: How can a galvanometer be converted into an ammeter? Write the expression for the shunt resistance.
questions.answer: A galvanometer of resistance G and full-scale current $I_g$ is converted into an ammeter by connecting a low resistance S (shunt) in parallel with it. The potential difference across both is the same: $I_gG = (I-I_g)S$. Hence $S = \frac{I_gG}{I-I_g}$, where I is the maximum current to be measured. The effective resistance of the ammeter is $\frac{GS}{G+S}$, which is very small.

questions.q: Derive an expression for the magnetic field at the centre of a circular current-carrying loop.
questions.answer: Consider a loop of radius R carrying current I. Take a small element $dl$ on the loop. By the Biot-Savart law the field at the centre is $dB = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{I\,dl\sin90^\circ}{R^2}$, since every element is perpendicular to the radius vector. All elements produce fields in the same direction (along the axis, given by the right-hand rule). $B = \frac{\mu_0I}{4\pi R^2}\oint dl = \frac{\mu_0I}{4\pi R^2}\times2\pi R$. Hence $B = \frac{\mu_0I}{2R}$. For N turns, $B = \frac{\mu_0NI}{2R}$.

questions.q: Derive an expression for the force per unit length between two long parallel current-carrying conductors.
questions.answer: Let wires a and b carry currents $I_a$ and $I_b$ in the same direction, separated by distance d. Field of wire a at wire b: $B_a = \frac{\mu_0I_a}{2\pi d}$, directed perpendicular to the plane of the wires. Force on a length l of wire b: $F_{ba} = I_bB_al = \frac{\mu_0I_aI_b}{2\pi d}l$, directed towards a (by Fleming's left-hand rule). Force per unit length: $\frac{F}{l} = \frac{\mu_0I_aI_b}{2\pi d}$. Parallel currents attract; antiparallel currents repel.
keywords: F/l = mu0 Ia Ib/2 pi d

questions.q: Using Ampere's circuital law, derive an expression for the magnetic field inside a long solenoid.
questions.answer: Consider a long solenoid with n turns per unit length carrying current I. Field outside is negligible and inside it is uniform and parallel to the axis. Take a rectangular Amperian loop abcd with side ab = h inside the solenoid, parallel to the axis. Along bc and da the field is perpendicular to the path (or zero), and along cd (outside) it is zero. So $\oint\vec{B}\cdot d\vec{l} = Bh$. Current enclosed $= nhI$. Ampere's law: $Bh = \mu_0nhI$. Hence $B = \mu_0nI$.

questions.q: A straight conductor of length 0.5 m carrying a current of 10 A is placed in a uniform magnetic field of 0.2 T making an angle of $30^\circ$ with the field. Find the force on the conductor.
questions.answer: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field: $F = BIl\sin\theta = 0.2\times10\times0.5\times\sin30^\circ = 1.0\times0.5 = 0.5$ N. The direction is perpendicular to both the conductor and the field, given by Fleming's left-hand rule.

questions.q: Derive an expression for the torque on a rectangular current loop placed in a uniform magnetic field. Hence write the expression for the magnetic dipole moment of the loop.
questions.answer: A rectangular loop of sides a and b with N turns carries current I in a uniform field B; the normal to the loop makes angle $\theta$ with B. Forces on the two sides of length b (perpendicular to B) are $F = IbB$ each, equal and opposite, and collinear along the axis, so they cancel without torque. Forces on the sides of length a are each $F = IaB$ (angle with B is 90 degrees), equal and opposite but not collinear: they form a couple with arm $b\sin\theta$. Torque $\tau = IaB\times b\sin\theta = IAB\sin\theta$ for one turn (A = ab); for N turns $\tau = NIAB\sin\theta$. In vector form $\vec{\tau} = \vec{m}\times\vec{B}$, where the magnetic moment $m = NIA$ (direction by right-hand rule). Torque is maximum when the plane of the loop is parallel to B and zero when perpendicular to B.
keywords: couple with arm b sin theta

questions.q: Describe the principle, construction and working of a cyclotron. Derive the expression for the cyclotron frequency.
questions.answer: Principle: a charged particle crossing an oscillating electric field repeatedly gains energy while a perpendicular magnetic field makes it move in circles; the time per revolution is independent of speed. Construction: two hollow semicircular metal dees D1 and D2 with a small gap, placed in a vacuum chamber between the poles of a strong electromagnet; a high-frequency alternating voltage is applied across the dees. Working: ions released at the centre are accelerated across the gap, enter a dee, describe a semicircle (field B perpendicular to the dees), and return to the gap just when the polarity has reversed, so they are accelerated again. The radius grows with speed and the ions spiral outward and are drawn out through a window. Magnetic force gives centripetal force: $qvB = \frac{mv^2}{r}$, so $r = \frac{mv}{qB}$. Time for half revolution $= \frac{\pi r}{v} = \frac{\pi m}{qB}$, independent of v. Cyclotron frequency $\nu_c = \frac{qB}{2\pi m}$. Maximum kinetic energy $K = \frac{q^2B^2R^2}{2m}$.

questions.q: Explain the principle, construction and working of a moving coil galvanometer. Define its current sensitivity.
questions.answer: Principle: a current-carrying coil placed in a uniform (radial) magnetic field experiences a torque. Construction: a rectangular coil of many turns of insulated copper wire wound on a soft-iron cylinder, suspended by a phosphor-bronze fibre between the concave pole pieces of a strong horseshoe magnet; the pole pieces and cylindrical core make the field radial, so the plane of the coil is always parallel to B. A pointer attached to the coil moves over a scale. Working: for current I the deflecting torque is $NIAB$. The suspension fibre gives a restoring torque $k\phi$, where k is the torsional constant and $\phi$ the deflection. At equilibrium $NIAB = k\phi$, so $\phi = \frac{NAB}{k}I$, i.e. deflection is proportional to current. Current sensitivity is the deflection per unit current: $\frac{\phi}{I} = \frac{NAB}{k}$. It increases with N, A, B and decreases with k.
keywords: torque on coil in radial field
